notes: How this part was researched: the session's web search allowance was already used up (200 of 200) before this part began, so no searching was possible at all. Pages were opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), robots.txt read first and obeyed (also for Anthropic's agent names). Filed campaign websites were read from sl_websites in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (read-only). Campaign sites nobody filed, local party units' pages and news reports could not be found without searching, so a blank here is not proof that nothing exists; a second pass with searching would be worth it.

Not read, and nothing worked around: kathykeena.com answered 403 to the kit's reader (the filed address stays as filed; nothing recorded from it); Dakota County's County Attorney address led only to a general Government page that does not name the County Attorney; mncourts.gov was not asked (it refuses scripts), so nothing for Judge Jeannice M. Reding; isd381.org answered with a redirect the reader does not follow; marshall.k12.mn.us showed no board page at the addresses tried; inver Grove Heights Schools' and Woodbury's member lists were not found at the addresses tried; the Republican Party of Minnesota's '2026 Republican Nominees' page carried no text naming Patty Bradway or A.J. Prospect, so no Republican endorsement is recorded for either. The Legislative Reference Library's name search is a form and was not used; Drew Christensen's record was reached by its plain address.

Checked and not found on their government's own list of today's office holders, so nothing recorded: Lonny Witkofsky (Itasca County lists Cory Smith for District 1), Thomas Opheim (Norman County lists Lee Ann Hall for District 4), Jeff Rowan (Monticello), Jenny Stuhr (Buffalo), Kevin Sethre (Inver Grove Heights), Joseph "JOE P." Petersen (Owatonna), Kristin Elizondo (Champlin lists Tom Moe for Ward 2), Ian Bergh (Willmar lists Rick Fagerlie and Justin Ask for Ward 3), Dan Solon (Elk River ISD 728), Gloria Colbenson (Monticello ISD 882; the district's page names her among the 2026 candidates), Brittany LaBore (ISD 622's election page calls only Caleb Anderson an incumbent). Martin County's site shows no page for a county surveyor, so nothing for Ben Madsen.

Left out on purpose: jobs, schools, family and party posts on the campaign sites; the private endorsements on Leah Hanson's and Drew Christensen's sites (not a party's own page); A.J. Prospect's site footer reads 'Republican Party of Minnesota' with no sentence around it, which is not an explicit statement, so no own_words. Start years of current terms are left blank where the government's page gives none.
